Functionalist understanding: Hype Studies as a Sociology of Expectations 2.0?

Expectations are functional for innovation systems:

• They are performative: stabilize orientation, attract interest, provide legitimation, foster investment.

• They coordinate actors across levels and contexts by linking present decisions to imagined futures.

• They turn promises into present obligations (“promise-requirement cycle”).

• They have a temporal pattern (“hype cycle”).

• They relate imagination & materiality.

Functional analysis examines what “problem” a phenomenon (expectations) solves for a system – how it organizes, stabilizes, or reproduces social order in different cases.

Hype as a communication problem: inappropriate exaggeration

RQ: What defines exaggeration from communication theoretical perspectives?

Exaggeration

Communicative goals

Exaggeration mechanism

Overgeneralization

Information

Underspecified or generic terms hinder accurate information transfer.

Over-selling

Persuasion

Malicious or bad rhetoric amplify benefits, urgency, or certainty.

Over-promising

Commitment

Speech enacts unreasonable promises and predictions.

Over-resonance

Social representation

Imitation and community norm alignment reinforce collective beliefs, credibility, and importance.

Over-shadowing

Attention & discourse power

Discourse amplifies some narratives at the expense of others.
